jurisdictions.ownership_note: Ownership is PARTIAL, in a way specific to this source. BORME publishes a company's ACTS: where a company has declared itself unipersonal, the gazette names its SOLE SHAREHOLDER (`Socio único: …`), and this slice returns that name with the act and the day it was published. What it does not publish is a cap table: no percentages, no shareholder register, and no beneficial owners. So for a single-member company the gazette names one owner, and for every other company it names none.

jurisdictions.ownership_note: Ownership is not public in this dataset, and it carries no people at all. Zefix is the CENTRAL BUSINESS NAME INDEX: it publishes the entity's name in each official language, its legal form, its UID and CH-ID, its registered address, its municipality and canton. The directors, the share capital and the shareholdings are filings made to the CANTONAL commercial registers and are not in this dataset in any field. So no owner, officer or shareholder can appear in an answer from this slice — and the absence of a person here is not evidence about who runs a company.

registers.name: Zefix — Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), Federal Commercial Registry Office (FCRO/EHRA), published as Linked Data on LINDAS
registers.licence: Zefix — Central Business Name Index (Zentraler Firmenindex), Federal Commercial Registry Office (FCRO/EHRA), Swiss Confederation, published as Linked Data on LINDAS (lindas.admin.ch). Licence: OGD Open use — must provide the source.

verifiable: company identity as the register publishes it: every official-language name of the entity (Nestlé S.A. / Nestlé AG / Nestlé Ltd. are ONE entity), the register's own id and its IRI
the SWISS UID (CHE-123.456.789) and the CH-ID (the old CH number), both exactly as the register publishes them — the UID only when its own modulus-11 check digit agrees

the legal form, as the publisher's own eCH-0097 code AND its own German label (Aktiengesellschaft, Gesellschaft mit beschränkter Haftung GMBH / SARL, Verein, Stiftung, Genossenschaft and the rest of the 38-form vocabulary)
the registered address (street, postal code, locality), the municipality and the canton
a lookup by registered name, in any official language, or by Swiss UID
that the entity is CURRENTLY ENTERED in the commercial register — that is what this core data holds
not_verifiable: directors, officers, shareholders and beneficial owners — Zefix is a name index; those are cantonal filings and appear in no field of this dataset
share capital, financial statements and annual accounts — not published in this dataset

the entity's STATUS — the core data carries no status field, so nothing here says whether an entity is trading, dormant or in liquidation (an entity whose NAME carries 'in Liquidation' says so in its name, and is still listed)
an entity that has been STRUCK OFF — deleted entries are dropped from the core data, so absence is NOT COVERED, never proof that a company never existed
a sole proprietorship below the registration threshold — it need not be entered in the commercial register at all, so it is NOT COVERED here
a CH-ID used as an identifier — it is published, but it is not a UID and this slice does not answer it as one

jurisdictions.ownership_note: Ownership is not in this dataset, and it carries no people at all. The Bolagsverket basic company data file publishes the organisation number and its type, every registered name, the organisation form, the registration date, any deregistration date and reason, any ongoing winding-up or restructuring proceeding, an activity description and the registered postal address. The board, the officers, the shareholders and the share capital are separate Bolagsverket products and appear in no field of this file. So no owner, officer or shareholder can appear in an answer from this slice — and the absence of a person here is not evidence about who runs a company.

registers.name: Bolagsverket — grunddata om företag (Swedish Companies Registration Office), bulk file published as an EU high-value dataset
registers.licence: Bolagsverket — grunddata om företag (high-value dataset), Swedish Companies Registration Office, bulk file bolagsverket_bulkfil.zip.

verifiable: company identity as the register publishes it: the registered name, every additional registered name, and each name's own type and registration date
the SWEDISH ORGANISATION NUMBER (XXXXXX-XXXX) exactly as the register publishes it — only when its own Luhn check digit agrees — and the identity type the publisher assigns it
the organisation form, as the publisher's own code AND its own Swedish label (Aktiebolag, Ekonomisk förening, Bostadsrättsförening, Handelsbolag, Stiftelse and the rest of the 29-form list)
the registration date, and — where the register has deregistered the organisation — the deregistration date and its reason, from the publisher's own 17-reason list
any ongoing winding-up or restructuring proceeding, with its own start date, from the publisher's own 11-code list
the activity description and the registered postal address (street, care-of, postal code, city, country)
a lookup by registered name, or by Swedish organisation number
not_verifiable: directors, board members, shareholders and beneficial owners — separate Bolagsverket products, and in no field of this file
share capital, financial statements and annual accounts — not published in this file
whether a company is TRADING or solvent — the file carries no trading status and no credit information; 'no deregistration recorded' is not a statement that the company is active
a sole trader identified by a PERSONAL identity number — this slice does not store, index or publish a personal identity number, so such a business is answerable by name only
a business that was never registered, or is registered with another authority — it is not in this file, so absence is NOT COVERED, never proof that a company never existed

price.fx_basis: ECB euro foreign exchange reference rates

jurisdictions.store_load: Its register is answered from an out-of-band store that holds NO loaded generation right now (se_register), so it cannot answer this register today — it is named NOT CONSULTED and answers `unknown`, never `not_found`. It is therefore NOT counted as live.

depth.note: SE is NOT on sale while it reads `data_pending`: its register is wired but cannot answer today, so a call returns `unknown` — and an unknown is not charged for. The depth band (7 verifiable items, deep) is published; the price is withheld, and the door refuses a call here rather than quoting one, until the register loads.

global_registers.note: Global legal-entity identifiers and Level 2 relationships. Consulted for identity and ownership edges wherever an entity has an LEI.

depth_ladder.unit: one entity check for one jurisdiction
depth_ladder.depth_rule: Depth is the number of items that jurisdiction's own coverage row lists as verifiable (the `verifiable` array on /coverage.json). The rung is chosen from that count.
depth_ladder.jurisdiction_rule: Name the jurisdiction to be quoted its rung (`?jurisdiction=AU`, or `jurisdiction` in the body). With none named, the country is read from the identifier's own shape, and the 402 says which was used.
depth_ladder.not_on_sale_rule: A jurisdiction whose register cannot answer today (status `data_pending`) is NOT on sale: it quotes no price and no rung, the door REFUSES the call rather than quoting one, and nothing is charged.
depth_ladder.mcp_note: The MCP tool `check_entity` is sold at the entry rung (US$0.10) whatever the jurisdiction's depth: the MCP gate prices a tool rather than an argument. The HTTP door quotes and settles the rung, and refuses a call that resolves deeper than the amount offered.

sanctions_registers.note: 1 of 5 advertised lists are NOT consulted: Australian Consolidated List (DFAT) (the store holds no generation for this list). Every answer names each of them as not consulted, and an absence verdict that depended on one is unknown rather than a clean result — the check is charged for what it read, not for what it did not.

ownership_summary: Ownership data — who ultimately owns or controls a company — is CLOSED in nearly every country we cover. We can honestly verify that a company exists, who runs it (where the register publishes it), and its status; in most of Europe we cannot yet verify who ultimately owns it. Each jurisdiction below says which side of that line it is on.

live_amounts.check_entity: US$0.10 (entry rung) to US$0.25 (10+ verifiable items)

charging.note: The entity check is priced by DEPTH: US$0.10 where a jurisdiction publishes 1-4 verifiable items, US$0.15 at 5-6, US$0.20 at 7-9 and US$0.25 at 10 or more (Australia, at 15). The depth and its price are printed side by side on every row above, on /pricing.md and on /health, and the door quotes the rung in its 402 BEFORE payment. A jurisdiction that cannot answer today is NOT on sale and quotes no price at all: a call naming one is refused with no amount and no payment requirement, because a call there answers `unknown` and an unknown is not charged for. The figure door is US$0.05 flat.
charging.how_it_is_charged: POST /entity quotes the rung of the jurisdiction the caller NAMES (`?jurisdiction=AU`, or `jurisdiction` in the body); with none named, the country is read from the identifier's own shape (an ABN is Australia, a SIREN France, and so on), and the 402 says which of the two it used. GET and HEAD on the same path quote the same rung. If the call resolves to a different depth, the door answers with a 402 naming the right rung and settles NOTHING for the refused attempt — nothing is ever charged above the rung the answer reaches.
charging.pack_rail: Prepaid pack credits are unchanged: one credit buys one entity call whatever its depth. That is the pack rail's existing discount, and /pricing.md states it.
